findings.body:
`middleware.RequireRole("admin")` was removed while mounting these handlers on the `/api/v2` subrouter. `GET /api/v2/admin/users` and `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` now call `listUsers` and `editRoles` with no role check, so any client that can reach the server can list users and change roles.

Keep the PathPrefix move and wrap both handlers with `authz` as before:

```suggestion
	v2.Handle("/admin/users", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.listUsers))).Methods("GET")
	v2.Handle("/admin/roles", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.editRoles))).Methods("POST")
```

Re-introduce `authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")` above the subrouter (or `v2.Use(authz)` on gorilla/mux). The repo has no other `RequireRole` (or handler-level) check that would cover these routes.

summary:
Admin routes moved under `/api/v2`, but `middleware.RequireRole("admin")` was dropped from both registrations. `GET /api/v2/admin/users` and `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` now run as unauthenticated handlers.

The PathPrefix subrouter itself is fine. Restore the `authz` wrap on both `Handle` calls (or `v2.Use(authz)` once on the subrouter) before merge. Callers of the old `/admin/*` paths will also need to switch to `/api/v2/admin/*` as part of this versioning move.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The base routes wrapped listUsers and editRoles with middleware.RequireRole("admin"); the head change mounts them on /api/v2 without that middleware or any other role check, so admin user-list and role-edit endpoints are unauthenticated.
